problem: Existing social-navigation and pedestrian-trajectory datasets are small, single-country or single-embodiment, lack explicit robot-crowd interaction (speech), and often lack human-verified metric-space trajectories, so models generalize poorly across cultures, locations and robot morphologies.
motivation: Social norms (passing side, personal space, proxemics) vary with culture, environment and robot embodiment, so data-driven social navigation and trajectory prediction need diverse, challenging, goal-directed real-world data. The authors pooled 8 teams in 5 countries to collect such data under common guidelines.
key_idea: Build a large multi-site, multi-embodiment social-navigation dataset that pairs goal-directed onboard robot data (including robot speech and scenario tags) with human-verified, metric-grounded overhead BEV pedestrian trajectories.
insight: Analyses show ACME contains harder scenes than SCAND/MuSoHu: TEB planner failures are 2x per minute and 4x per 5 m versus SCAND, even though Hausdorff distance to expert paths is similar. Trajectory predictors degrade on ACME (ADE/FDE up ~0.1/0.15 m vs ETH/UCY, and ~0.38/0.72 m on dynamic-only), and BEV data reveal culture-linked passing-side preferences that follow local driving side (right in US/Germany, left tendency in Japan/Singapore). Robot speech usage depends on embodiment and operation mode (teleoperated vs human-accompanied).
method: Multi-site collection: 8 teams in 5 countries, 7 embodiments (Unitree Go2/Go1, suitcase robots, Stretch 2, Shadow, Scout Mini) with common sensor minimum (odometry, egocentric RGB, 3D LiDAR, calibration) and ROS2 bags.

Teleoperation guidelines: Wizard-of-Oz distance, restricted speech set (Excuse Me / Attention Robot Here / Please Give Way), fixed goal before each trajectory, Begin/Discard/End markers to segment short goal-directed trajectories.
BEV trajectory annotation: ByteTrack on overhead cameras followed by human verification at 10 Hz with a custom tool (Relabel, Missing, Break, Join, Delete, Disentangle, Undo).
Metric grounding: image-to-ground homographies via AprilTags or measured keypoints; cleaning (drop <3.2 s, jump fix, smoothing, stationary labeling, ±25 m crop); ETH/UCY-format release at 2.5 Hz.

Tagging: manual scenario tags for robot trajectories (12 tags) and semantic BEV scene masks (corridors, open areas, intersections, blind corners); anonymization (none/face blur/full-body mask) with released detections/keypoints.

Analysis and benchmarks: pedestrian density, SAM2-based traversability, TEB planner comparison, ViNT/NoMaD benchmark, five trajectory predictors, cross-culture speed/passing-side/personal-space analyses.

setting.backbone: Dataset paper; benchmarks pretrained ViNT and NoMaD (evaluated as-is) and trajectory predictors SocialGAN, AgentFormer, SGNet, TUTR, MoFlow trained on ETH/UCY
setting.training_data: Dataset contribution: 29.35 h onboard robot data and 43.5 h BEV pedestrian tracking (72.1K trajectories); benchmarked predictors trained on ETH/UCY only; ViNT/NoMaD used pretrained
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB(D), 3D LiDAR, odometry, robot speech logs, plus overhead BEV camera video
setting.action_space: Human-teleoperated or human-guided robot trajectories (recorded odometry); benchmarks predict waypoints

numbers.extra: Waypoint-prediction alignment to expert trajectories, not a navigation success benchmark

numbers.eval_set_note: whole ACME BEV dataset; models trained on ETH/UCY
numbers.extra: Trained on ETH/UCY, best-of-20 ADE/FDE; 8 obs / 12 pred steps at 2.5 Hz

numbers_note: Dataset paper; no navigation success-rate benchmarks. Other predictors' ACME numbers (e.g., AgentFormer 0.30/0.58) are baselines and omitted.
results: ACME provides 29.35 h robot data and 43.5 h BEV data (72.1K trajectories, ~4x the duration of TBD). It is harder than SCAND/MuSoHu (TEB fails 2x/min and 4x/5 m vs SCAND). All trajectory predictors degrade versus ETH/UCY (e.g., MoFlow 0.21/0.41 to 0.31/0.59; 0.54/1.06 on dynamic-only), and ViNT/NoMaD are worse than on SCAND.
limitations: Only some sites have accurate map-based localization, so BEV trajectories can't yet be projected into robot egocentric view; anonymization levels differ across sites
Culture is confounded with site, environment and embodiment (7 of 8 sites are university campuses; one robot per location), so cultural conclusions are indirect
Homography via AprilTags is imprecise and far pedestrians are cropped; only ETH/UCY-trained predictors and pretrained navigation models are benchmarked
